resources.string: Speak instead of typing
Tap the microphone in the message box and talk: a live waveform and a timer show that you are being heard. Confirm to keep the text, or cancel to drop it.
A finger taps the microphone, the message box shows a moving waveform with a timer, then the spoken sentence appears as text.
Better dictation with a cloud model
Pick a provider and a transcription model in the settings. The recording is sent when you stop, and the text lands in the message box for you to check.
A finger chooses Cloud as speech to text, then a recording is transcribed and the text appears in the message box.
Settings, easy to find
Settings are grouped into categories, each with its own page. Not sure where something lives? Search for it and jump straight to the setting.
A finger opens the Voice input category, goes back, then types in the search field and the matching settings are listed.
More room for the terminal
Enter full screen to hide the title bar and the system bars and see more lines at once. Back or the same button brings them back.
A finger taps the full screen button of the terminal: the title bar and the status bar slide away and more output lines appear.
Switch model without waiting
Change the agent or the model while a reply is still running: the change applies with your next message. New chats start from the model you used last.
While the assistant is working, a finger opens the model menu and picks another model; a note says it applies to the next message.
One row for a chain of thoughts
Consecutive thoughts of the assistant are grouped into a single row that is easy to scan. Tap it to read each thought.
Three separate thought rows merge into one row, which a finger taps to show the three thoughts.
Peek at the chat while you decide
Question and permission cards fold down to a slim bar, so you can read the conversation before answering. Tap the bar to open the card again.
A permission card is folded to a bar with a tap on its arrow, and opened again by tapping the bar.
See what is running, live
A chip above the message box counts the subagents and background commands that are running. Open it to follow their time and output, or stop them.
A finger taps the running chip and a sheet lists a subagent and a command with a ticking timer and a Stop button.
